newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land shrugs off weak Sing dollar.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land shrugs off weak Sing dollar.

text.p: Property blue chip DBS Land said the weakening of the Singapore dollar will not affect its operations or expansion plans in the Asia-Pacific region, Deputy Chairman Han Cheng Fong said.

The Singapore dollar had slid to a low on Friday of 1.5245 to the U.S. dollar, following on the heels of the battering from speculative attacks sustained by other regional currencies like the Indonesian rupiah and the Malaysian ringgit.
"The answer is none," Han said when asked what effect the falling Singapore unit will have on their operations or overseas expansion plans. "We will continue to buy."
Company secretary Lim Joke Mui said gyrations of regional currencies will have a minimal impact on their operations amounting to about Singapore $2.5 million.
The turnover of the company in the first half of 1997 alone reached S$415.30 million, up 5.3 percent from the first half in the previous year.

A unit of DBS Land, Raffles Holdings, plans to open two hotels in Cambodia in the last quarter of 1997. There are also various projects in Hong Kong, China and Indonesia that will come on stream later in the year.
DBS Land is also involved in residential projects through its Australian subsidiary, Australand.
